title: Tenant KV swapback throttle and deadlock scratchpad
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is an incident synthesis + emergent runbook draft focused on a recurring class of serving-runtime failures we saw in Oct–Nov: host-level OOMs correlated with long-running kv cache swapback operations that sometimes result in micro-deadlocks between the prefetch/eviction subsystem and the swapback coordinator. Audience: SREs on-call for serving runtime, oncall triage engineers, and the runtime devs investigating KV lifecycle semantics.

Executive summary:
- Symptom: periodic multi-tenant host OOMs during high contended prefix churn, often immediately after rolling deployments or sustained traffic spikes.
- Immediate impact: degraded tail latency and partial capacity loss on affected pool; some tenants saw 5–10% increased token drop rate during incidents.
- Root-cause hypothesis (current): a timing window where swapback (spill-to-disk / reclaim pipeline) holds a host-wide lock while prefetch threads push new KV entries and eviction tries to demote items. Under heavy churn, swapback becomes a backpressure point, blocking eviction/gc, which causes memory amplification and eventual host OOM. In some runs we observed a second factor: swapback retry thrashing that temporarily clones buffers leading to transient memory spike.
- Status: draft runbook below + set of experiments to validate swapback lock granularity and retry backoff.

Detection signals (what tripped first in observed incidents):
- heap_growth: host_heap_bytes shows sustained slope > 200MB/min for > 3 minutes.
- kv_swapback_queue_depth > 50 for > 2m and swapback_latency_p95 > 15s.
- microbatch_queue_length oscillation + request_tail_latency spikes (p99) contemporaneous with heap slope.
- evict_attempts_failures and prefetch_queue_rejects increase; logs show repeated "swapback: holding swap token" messages.
- OOM killer events in host kernel or process-level OOMs in runtime during final phase.

Quick triage checklist (for on-call):
1) Evaluate scope: check telemetry dashboard for pool X and host list. If more than 25% of hosts in pool show swapback_queue_depth > 50, escalate to SRE lead.
2) Temporarily reduce incoming load for affected tenants (route to fallback pool / scale up dedicated pool) — use routing policy id RTE-evict-01 in Console.
3) If host process still alive but heap slope > threshold, trigger "eviction-hold-skip" hotpatch (k8s: annotate runtime pods with runtime.redwood.io/eviction-skip=true) to force synchronous eviction cycles (see infra SOP). This is a blunt instrument — only use if degraded service is unacceptable.
4) If pods are unresponsive / OOMing, cordon and restart hosts one at a time to avoid correlated rolling failure.
5) Collect diagnostic artifacts before restart: /var/log/serving-runtime/kvswap.log*, pprof heap snapshot, dmesg, and an aggregated trace (trace id in runtime logs). Upload to incident folder and link to Linear ticket.

Mitigations applied during last incident (what worked / partial wins):
- Short term (2–6 hours): applied per-tenant route throttles + temporarily bumped dedicated pool capacity — reduced the pressure on swapback queue and allowed the backlog to drain.
- Medium term (24–72 hours): pushed a hotfix that added exponential backoff to swapback retries, which removed the repeated buffer duplications and lowered the max transient memory spike.
- Not effective: naively increasing swapback worker count without lock redesign increased contention and made host instability worse.

Evidence and diagnostics (summary of collected artifacts):
- pprof heap: multiple large retained objects rooted via "swapback.buffer::pending_copy" in hosts A/B/C.
- logs: series of interleaved lines where swapback coordinator logs "acquire swap token" and eviction threads log "waiting on swap token" for ~10–30s windows.
- kernel messages: oom_reaper invoked on runtime pid twice; no host-level killing of other processes observed.
- metric correlation: swapback_latency_p95 correlated with host_heap_slope at r=0.82 across incidents.

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Lock granularity: swapback holds a coarse lock across multiple tenant partitions while copying pages out; eviction/prefetch must wait, amplifying memory pressure.
B) Retry/error path duplication: failed swapback attempts duplicate buffers in transient heap region when a retry path re-allocates without freeing previous partial state.
C) Ordering inversion: a prefetch thread enqueues a large sequence of new KV entries while swapback enumerates structures, causing temporary double-accounting.
D) Scheduling/CPU starvation: under high host CPU load, swapback latencies blow up; backpressure isn't applied to prefetch fast-path, so memory grows faster than swapback can reclaim.

Planned experiments (to run in staging):
- E1: Decrease swapback lock scope to per-tenant partition (instrumentation flags only) and replay production-like churn for 6 hours. Measure swapback_latency and heap_slope.
- E2: Enable protective reservation: when swapback_queue_depth > 20, reject new prefetches for lower priority tenants and see if heap stabilizes.
- E3: Add guard on retry path to free partial buffers before re-allocating; run pprof and assert no duplicate roots.
- E4: CPU throttling simulation to confirm whether scheduling delays are amplifying the problem.

Runbook draft (procedural and explicit, for inclusion in the SRE playbook):
Trigger condition: swapback_queue_depth > 50 AND host_heap_slope > 150MB/min for 3 contiguous minutes.

Immediate steps (0–15m):
- Step 0: Pager to SRE on-call. Post to #sre-runtime with a brief summary and affected pool.
- Step 1: Run diagnostics script: /scripts/collect-kvswap-diagnostics.sh <host> -> saves pprof + logs to /tmp/incident-<id>. Tarball and upload.
- Step 2: If single host only: cordon host and restart runtime pod. If >3 hosts, consider routing throttle at pool level.
- Step 3: If swapback log shows repeated "retry" errors, toggle feature-flag runtime.swapback.retry_backoff=true via dynconfig.

Recovery steps (15–90m):
- Validate memory slope across hosts trending down. If not: escalate to runtime team for immediate patch (retry backoff / free-before-realloc).
- Re-enable prefetch for tenants incrementally after stability for 10m windows.

Longer-term fixes (postmortem action items):
- Replace coarse lock with partitioned lock (owner: Marco Alvarez, GH PR: linked). Target: Q1 2026.
- Add automatic prefetch throttling when swapback_queue_depth > threshold (owner: Jia Lin).
- Add safety net: reject prefetches from non-plat tenants when host_heap is above X% of alloc (owner: SRE infra).
- Add more guardrails in metrics to auto-scale pool when swapback saturates (owner: product/infra).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Is the buffer duplication purely in user-space code, or are we seeing kernel-level copy-on-write bursts from large mmap ranges? Need memmap traces to prove.
- Can we change the retry policy without risking data loss under swapback transient errors?
- Is it safe to annotate pods to skip eviction cycles long-term? Risk: memory fragmentation.

Notes to runtime engineers (implementation hints):
- Look at swapback code path: pay attention to "pending_copy" lifetimes. Add explicit free/clear in all early return branches.
- Instrument lock acquisition times with tenant/partition tags. We need a short label on traces for correlating with tenant churn.
- Add a circuit-breaker guarding allocation size per-swapback operation to fail fast instead of retrying.

Follow-ups and owners (concrete tickets):
- RW-7821: Expand swapback instrumentation and add partitioned locking experiment (owner: Marco Alvarez) — blocker: needs infra testing environment.
- RW-7857: Implement retry_backoff and partial-buffer-free patch (owner: Jia Lin).
- RW-7890: Auto-throttle prefetch in console routing (owner: SRE infra / product).

Appendix: quick commands (internal)
- collect diagnostics: sudo /scripts/collect-kvswap-diagnostics.sh host-12 > /tmp/diag.tar.gz
- force drain: curl -XPOST "https://console.internal/pools/POOLX/drain?reason=kvswap-pressure" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- toggle dynconfig: curl -XPOST https://dynconfig.internal/v1/set -d '{"key":"runtime.swapback.retry_backoff","value":true}'

Incident postmortem checklist for PM/Stakeholders:
- Provide a short incident blurb for weekly "platform health" with impact (hosts affected, customer-visible latency increase, mitigation steps taken).
- Confirm timelines for code fixes and next runbook revision.

Rough timeline summary for last incident (for context):
- T0: 2025-11-03 02:12 UTC: alert fired for heap_slope; swapback backlog rising.
- T+12m: throttles applied to top 5 tenants, swapback queue stops growing but latency remains high.
- T+45m: two hosts OOM and were restarted; partial capacity loss.
- T+6h: retry_backoff flag enabled; memory slope reduced and pool recovered.

This document is intentionally an iterative scratchpad. If you are reading this and have data or test results relevant to hypotheses E1–E4, paste notes below or attach pprof snapshots via the Linear ticket.

Recent edits: 2025-11-20 — added runbook triggers and experiment list (Ravi).
